passage:
A new light rail line opened in the city. It connected neighborhoods that had long depended on buses and scooters.
Some people praised it for reducing traffic. Others complained about construction delays and noise during building.
A student interviewed residents for a report. Older residents liked easier travel to hospitals. Shop owners near stations saw more customers. Drivers worried about losing road space.
The student's report did not call the project simply good or bad.
Transportation changes daily life in many directions. A rail line is not only tracks and trains. It is time, business, access, and the shape of a city's future.
